descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-92586 AC 7, AC 10 · “Handoff can only be sent to a signed-in, valid recipient, not an arbitrary email address”. Mixed: stated part — An email-address recipient refused; the picker shows no list of all users; our part — Send to self, empty text, an outsider or bogus id reading a handoff (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Approach · TC-08 Handoff Summary · S07 Existing api specs: who can send to whom and who can read it — colleague delivered; self, email address, empty text refused; an outsider and a mistyped id get nothing

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U5 The handoff is generated and delivered entirely in-app, only to a signed-in, valid Round Companion recipient (another physician's account), never to an arbitrary email address; … (UAT TC-08; TFA-92586 AC 6; TFA-92586 AC 7) — gate: blocked: TFA-92586 ready for pr
  • U6 Every sent handoff leaves a persistent record (sender, recipient, timestamp) that both the sender and the recipient can retrieve. (UAT TC-08; TFA-92586 AC 8) — gate: blocked: TFA-92586 ready for pr

Test design technique: Decision table (decision-table) — List the combinations of several conditions and check each one, to see that the result follows the rule.

Given Three accounts: sender, recipient and an outsider (CONTEXT_USER)

When Send to self, to 'someone@example.com', with whitespace text; list recipients; the outsider fetches the handoff by id, lists inbox and sent and tries markRead; the sender fetches a bogus id

Then Self → 'not to yourself'; email string → 'not a RoundCompanion user'; empty → 'nothing to hand off'; picker rows are {userId, name} only, never the caller; the outsider gets null / no rows / 'Handoff not found'; a bogus id returns null, no crash. Colleague row is S05; disabled-account row is S19

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Table from AC 7 ('only a signed-in, valid recipient, not an arbitrary email address') and AC 8 ('retrievable by both sender and recipient', no one else): every non-account destination refused and every outsider read empty, server-side; Playwright assertions. Not in the table: a header-only, zero-patient sheet is accepted by the server (only whitespace is refused), see risks

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method API · API (Convex functions); lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (automated)
